clue.text: Nick's favourite dog

parts.note: to nick something is to steal it, and to whip is slang for the same
a favourite, especially an animal, is a pet

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick has a favourite breed of dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name; it is the verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippet is a slender racing breed similar to a small greyhound.

clue.text: My wish for something fancy

definitions.note: a whimsical thing, the clue leaning on 'fancy' to colour it

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine, so these letters are freely reimagined

explanation.surface: Someone's wish is for something fanciful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges MY WISH and also colours the definition, so 'something fancy' reads as the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim or fanciful notion is a playful, quaint idea of this kind.

clue.text: Needing support in business

parts.note: taken as written
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: A company that needs backing to stay afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frail through age or illness needs to lean on help or a stick.

clue.text: Repair with help involving minor

indicators.note: the two words are involved, wound together, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A minor repair job that needs some help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' mixes REPAIR and HELP together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the edge of a matter is of lesser importance, hence secondary.

clue.text: Refuse to start treating skin problem

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak on the skin

explanation.surface: A patient declines to begin treating a skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb meaning decline; it is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun is waste or rubbish, which Americans call trash.

clue.text: Knew what was expected

parts.note: knowing in advance what is going to happen is having seen it coming

explanation.surface: Someone was unsurprised because they knew the expected outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To have predicted events is to have known beforehand what was coming.

clue.text: Unusual forenames for a lodger?

definitions.note: a member of a lodge, not a tenant

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of letters is not their normal order

explanation.surface: A boarder with strange first names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges FORENAMES. 'lodger' looks like a tenant; here it is someone belonging to a lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the fraternal society meet in local chapters called lodges, so one is a lodge member.

clue.text: First rider on a new horse

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
new letters are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: The first person to ride a newly acquired horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ON A into OAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat has white hairs mixed with a base colour.

clue.text: Small sum of money sent round as deposit

indicators.note: the word sent goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
a dime is a ten-cent coin, a small sum in the US

explanation.surface: A modest amount of cash posted as a down payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' looks like a payment, as the surface says; it is matter that settles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles out of a liquid, a deposit at the bottom.

clue.text: After no peace I head for caution

indicators.note: the pieces for I and head come after the one for no peace

parts.note: where there is no peace there is war
taken as written
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Sheerness

explanation.surface: After the war ends, someone heads forward cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland or promontory, common in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary means being cautious and on guard.

clue.text: Gather in and iron, right?

parts.note: taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Domestic chores: gathering clothes in and ironing them, is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' looks like collecting laundry; here it means deduce.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather in the sense of conclude from evidence is to deduce.

clue.text: A channel swimmer accepts kiss from the great man

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one word accepting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont channel nightly to visit Hero
X is the conventional written kiss

explanation.surface: A cross-Channel swimmer receives a kiss from a famous man.
explanation.walkthrough: The channel is not the English Channel but the Hellespont, the strait Leander swam.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander of Macedon is known to history as Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Heroes camp out but return to base with difficulty

indicators.note: letters that are out are put out of their usual order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Heroes break camp but struggle to get back to their base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HEROES CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape home is an idiom for winning or arriving by the narrowest margin.

clue.text: Being awkward, mean to get the last word

indicators.note: letters being awkward are unruly, so they fall into a different order

explanation.surface: A contrary person is mean just so they can have the last word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being awkward' rearranges MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing word said at the end of a prayer or hymn, literally its final word.

clue.text: Makes effective tools

definitions.meaning: puts a plan into action, carries it out
instruments or utensils used for work

explanation.surface: Effective tools get the job done.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means carries out a plan; the noun means instruments for working.

clue.text: Snacks for new students in rest break

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
to break something is to smash it up, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: first-year university students are freshmen

explanation.surface: Snacks laid on for freshers during a rest break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest break' reads as one phrase, a pause; in fact 'break' scrambles the word before it into RETS, the case that 'in' fills.
explanation.definitionFit: Light food and drinks offered at an event are snacks of this kind.

clue.text: Wild winds rose, bringing violent disturbance

indicators.note: wild letters run out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: Fierce gales rose, causing a violent storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges WINDS ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy, rough and disorderly behaviour is a disturbance of the peace.

clue.text: Helps to define the goal of angry lawyers

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing what the noun answer does

parts.note: cross means angry
the bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Irate lawyers help set out what their aim is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' looks like an aim; it is the frame in football.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizontal beam across the top of the posts marks the upper limit of a football goal.

clue.text: False encouragement given on debts

indicators.note: in a down clue the debts piece sits on top of, after, the other

parts.note: a spur is an incentive or encouragement
IOUs are written acknowledgments of debts

explanation.surface: Insincere encouragement given to people in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious things are fake or not genuine, though they look plausible.

clue.text: Rent vehicle plant that was dormant for a long period

definitions.text: that was dormant for a long period
definitions.note: a description standing for a person, the one who slept for years

parts.note: rent as the past of rend means torn, as is a rip
a van is a road vehicle
winkle is short for periwinkle, a name shared by a trailing plant and a sea snail

explanation.surface: Hiring a vehicle to carry a plant that lay dormant for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a hiring payment; it is the past tense of rend, torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington Irving's character sleeps for twenty years in the Catskill mountains and wakes to a changed world.

clue.text: Good man, competent and reliable

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint, a good man
able means competent

explanation.surface: A good man who is capable and dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steady and secure can be relied upon.

clue.text: Trophies of victory for the brave

definitions.text: Trophies of victory for the brave

parts.words: Trophies of victory for the brave
parts.note: brave here is the old term for a Native American warrior, who took these from enemies

explanation.surface: Prizes for courageous winners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective for courageous people; it is the noun for a warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors traditionally cut the skin and hair from a slain enemy's head as a trophy.

clue.text: Island needing second rescue vessel

parts.note: Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: An island that needs a second lifeboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between Guernsey and Jersey.

clue.text: Tactful negotiator in charge

parts.note: a diplomat negotiates between nations

explanation.surface: A tactful negotiator is put in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful and sensitive in dealing with people, as envoys must be.

clue.text: Criminal file that's wrong, then put right

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: An incorrect criminal file gets corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's wrong' rearranges FILE into LIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a life sentence is a convicted criminal.

clue.text: To be taken advantage of isn't new

explanation.surface: Being exploited is no novelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploited people have been put to use; second-hand goods have been put to use before.

clue.text: It normally has its contents back to front

definitions.text: It normally has its contents back to front

parts.words: It normally has its contents back to front
parts.note: volumes stand with their spines facing outwards, so the backs are at the front

explanation.surface: Something that keeps everything it holds the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' suggests reversal, but means the spines of the volumes show at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A library shelf holds volumes with their spines, their backs, facing the reader.

clue.text: This prize brings back the good in French language

indicators.note: bringing words back means reading them from the end to the start

parts.note: in French, the good is le bon

explanation.surface: A prize that restores the good in the French language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings back' turns LE BON around.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish-founded awards for peace, literature and the sciences are the best-known international prizes.

clue.text: Lives in des res I converted

indicators.note: a converted building is remodelled, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lives in a desirable residence they converted themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'des res' is British estate-agent slang for a desirable residence; 'converted' rearranges it with I.
explanation.definitionFit: To live somewhere is to dwell or have one's home there.

clue.text: More than one slice of the right allotment of shares

indicators.note: an allotment of shares deals them out afresh, so the letters are redistributed

explanation.surface: Your rightful portion of the shares, sliced up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allotment of' rearranges SHARES into ASHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashers are thin slices, usually of bacon, so the plural fits several slices.
